children.value: This Notebook shows introduces the basic concepts of RDDs and operations on them visually, by showing the contents of the RDDs as a table.
The following helper functions displays the current contents of an RDD (partition-by-partition). This is best used for small RDDs with manageable number of partitions.

class DisplayRDD: def __init__(self, rdd): self.rdd = rdd def _repr_html_(self): x = self.rdd.mapPartitionsWithIndex(lambda i, x: [(i, [y for y in x])]) l = x.collect() s = "{}
".format("".join(["Partition {}".format(str(j)) for (j, r) in l])) s += ''.join(["
  • {}
".format("
  • ".join([str(rr) for rr in r])) for (j, r) in l]) s += "
    • " return s
Lets start with some basic operations using a small RDD to visualize what’s going on. We will create a RDD of Strings, using the
file which contains a list of the state names.
The notebook has already initialized a SparkContext, and we can refer to it as
to create this RDD. This operations reads the file and treats every line as a separate object. We will use DisplayRDD() to visualize it. The second argument of
is the number of partitions. We will set this as 10 to get started. If we don’t do that, Spark will only create a single partition given the file is pretty small.

children.value: Finally, lets look at an example of joins. We will still use small RDDs, but we now need two of them. We will just use

to create those RDDs. That functions takes in a list and creates an RDD of that by creating partitions and splitting them across machines. It takes the number of partitions as the second argument (optional).
Note again that Spark made no attempt to co-locate the objects (i.e., the tuples) with the same key.

children.value: Here is the definition of join from the programming guide.

When called on datasets of type (K, V) and (K, W), returns a dataset of (K, (V, W)) pairs with all pairs of elements for each key. Outer joins are supported through leftOuterJoin, rightOuterJoin, and fullOuterJoin.
We want to join on the first attributes, so we can just call join directly, otherwise a map may have been required.
